title: Will there actually be a Fred Astaire biopic?

commenti.body:
When Ginger Rogers was awarded at the Kennedy Center Honors, Fred Astaire’s widow did not allow clips of him to be used in the commemorative video of her career. Ginger Roger still made many movies and had a career of her own, it was not the least upsetting they made 10 movies together!

That being said I don’t know how it really works with biopics; while Elizabeth Taylor was alive she fought every try they had and at one point they did make one in the 90s, and she was completely against it. So at the end of the day if they want to I guess they’ll just do.

Wow, that seems really petty (ETA: of his widow).

For sure, GR had an interesting life and successful career in her own right, and I'd watch any film documenting it. I just wonder if it's too hard a sell without the canonized Fred & Ginger magic. Plus, if there's drama to be mined (like that Kennedy Center tidbit you cited),  that kind of thing is too tantalizing to the powers-that-be to not pull on that thread.

Tom Holland played Billy Elliott in the Elton John musical; the lyricist and book author will write this adaptation so it looks promising. The other has the actor from the movie. Personality rights would prevent an anaurhorized film for a long time, afaik, because Fred Astaire wasn't a politician. It would be shortsighted for the estate to not want to profit from and influence a depiction made now, instead of one coming out many decades later.
It is many decades later.  His last film was in 1981 and he died in 87.  He was on broadway a century ago.  At this point I can’t see anybody willing to pay a lot to get the inside scoop on his life.
William Hearst actively fought Citizen Kane whilst being alive

In California the personality rights last 70 years. So the estate has a strong position to negotiate from. It would probably be best to make the movies now, considering younger generations are less likely to know about him. But it's s not necessarily now or never.

That Fosse fx series was awful. The lead actor was big at the time. But incapable of good jazz dance. He’s embarrassingly bad at it. I realize people not acquainted with jazz dance have a different mood. But as a trained jazz dancer, he’s terrible. Jazz dance is intricate, there are certain rules. It’s a gorgeous mixture of stripper moves, a little ballet. The lead actor clearly didn’t take long enough to study. I commend Natalie Portman for taking the time to learn ballet for her role in Black Swan. An actor would have to spend a full year learning to dance to play that role. Commit. Daily lessons and classes.
